objects.description: Establish an evidence-backed map of how work is currently planned, tracked and remembered here, so that the model that replaces it is built against reality rather than against the README.

objects.title: Define the canonical milestone and issue schema
objects.description: Define the smallest repository-native representation of a milestone outcome specification and an issue execution contract, and enforce it the way every other configuration file here is enforced: a key nobody reads is an error.

objects.title: Implement the model loader and the status derivation engine
objects.description: Load every canonical file into one normalised model and derive issue and milestone status from recorded facts, in exactly one implementation that every surface calls.

objects.title: Implement DAG validation and execution waves
objects.description: Validate the dependency graph and derive topological execution waves, refusing every malformed graph with a named finding rather than a guess.

objects.title: Implement the plan command surface
objects.description: Give a worker one command that answers what is ready, why something is blocked, what the graph looks like, and that moves an issue through its lifecycle while refusing illegal transitions.

objects.title: Generate the Mermaid DAG from the graph
objects.description: Render the dependency graph as Mermaid from the same edges the engine derives, so that no diagram anywhere is drawn by hand.

objects.title: Enforce the canonical model as doctrine
objects.description: Add the project model to the doctrine registry so that doctor reports a broken model and watch reports a model that has drifted, through the same dispatcher every other rule uses.

objects.title: Project the model to GitHub milestones and issues
objects.description: Create and update GitHub milestones and issues from the canonical model, report drift instead of overwriting human edits, and keep every network call out of the tool itself.

objects.title: Project the model into the website
objects.description: Generate the roadmap, every milestone page, every issue page and the DAG page from the canonical model through the existing site data pipeline.

objects.title: Behavioural tests for schema, status, graph and command
objects.description: Prove each rule of the model with a case that fails when the rule is removed, in a disposable repository, the way every other rule here is proven.

objects.title: Cross-surface consistency and mutation tests
objects.description: Prove that the CLI, the generated site data and the GitHub projection describe the same graph, and that changing one canonical dependency changes all of them.

objects.title: Make CI refuse an invalid model or a stale projection
objects.description: Add the model validation and the projection freshness check to the blocking CI job, with no advisory pass.

objects.title: Document the semantics and the dogfooding rule
objects.description: Write the human documentation that explains why the model exists and what its terms mean, and leave every current fact to be generated.

objects.title: Make the worker instructions require the model
objects.description: Change the always-loaded provider instructions so that a fresh worker of any provider selects work through the model rather than from conversation or a TODO list.

objects.title: Open the first real milestone and execute one issue through it
objects.description: Prove the system on real repository work: open a milestone that exists because the repository needs it, and take one of its issues from READY to DONE entirely through the model.

objects.title: Reproduce the escaped blocker as an executable case
objects.description: Write a behavioural case that runs the documented sequence — open a question, hand over, start a new task, finish completed — and records what happens today, so that the gap stops being a sentence in a claim note and becomes something a command demonstrates.

objects.title: Decide whether a question transfers or the gate widens
objects.description: Choose between the two alternatives the claim names, record the decision with what was rejected and why, and state which case the chosen behaviour is deliberately wrong in.

objects.title: Implement the decision and prove it holds
objects.description: Make the chosen behaviour real in the question store and the blocker gate, and turn the characterisation case from I0101 into a case that fails when the behaviour is removed.

objects.title: Move the claim from planned to guaranteed
objects.description: Update docs/CLAIMS.yaml and the claim's detail page so the public surface states what is now true, with the file that implements it and the test that proves it.

objects.title: Declare which profile axis may become which runtime limit
objects.description: Add one canonical file beside the profiles that maps a profile axis to the runtime limit it may derive, so that a limit has a single source, an axis nobody can enforce cannot be listed, and a limit no adapter applies is a validation error rather than a comment.

objects.title: Resolve a task's effective limits and print them as data
objects.description: Add a read-only command that resolves the limits the active task's profile derives and prints them, in text and as JSON, so that a worker, a wrapper or a test can read the same numbers the enforcement will use.

objects.title: Make enforcement opt-in, and prove a repository that declines is unaffected
objects.description: Add one policy key that turns runtime enforcement on, default it to off, and prove with a case that a repository which never sets it behaves exactly as it does today.

objects.title: Apply one derived limit for real and prove it changes what happens
objects.description: Implement the first adapter: one limit, derived from the profile through the resolver, applied where a provider can honestly apply it, with a behavioural case that fails if the limit stops being applied.

objects.title: Declare the clamp as a doctrine so the mapping and the adapter cannot drift
objects.description: Declare the rule that every applied limit is derived from the declared mapping as a doctrine with its own validator, dispatched from the registry, reaching the command that claims to run it, covered by a case and run in CI.

objects.title: Publish the runtime-adapters claim with the test that proves it and the limits it does not cover
objects.description: Move the runtime-adapters row from planned to guaranteed, citing the adapter and the case, and state on its detail page which axes remain advisory and why, so that the guarantee is narrower than the milestone title rather than as wide as it.

objects.title: Define the execution record, including what an absence looks like
objects.description: Define the durable shape of a task's execution facts: which fields exist, who reported each one, and how a provider that reported nothing is recorded, so that absence is a value with a reason rather than a missing key or a zero.

objects.title: Record telemetry a provider reports, and refuse anything it did not
objects.description: Add the command that attaches measured execution facts to the active task, accepting only values a provider actually reported and refusing any field the caller cannot attribute to a reporter.

objects.title: Prove a silent provider produces an explicit absence, never a guess
objects.description: Write the case that runs a whole task under a provider that reports nothing and asserts that the completed record carries an explicit absence with a reason, and that no field anywhere in the surfaces shows an estimated number.

objects.title: Read the measurements back through the history surface, under a bound
objects.description: Make recorded execution facts readable through the surface that already answers questions about past tasks, with the same retention bound the other durable stores carry.

objects.title: Publish the telemetry claim and record what remains unmeasured
objects.description: Move the telemetry claim to guaranteed for the providers that report honestly, name the implementation and the case, and state in the economics document which providers report nothing and what that costs the analysis.

objects.title: Define an accepted outcome, and join it to its measurements without storing the join
objects.description: Define precisely which finishes count as accepted outcomes, and derive the join between an accepted outcome and the execution facts of the work that produced it from records that already exist, storing no third record.

objects.title: Report cost only where measurement and acceptance both exist
objects.description: Add the command that reports what accepted outcomes cost, computed only from measured facts, and reports no figure at all where either half is missing, saying which half.

objects.title: Make a thin denominator say so rather than average it away
objects.description: Make every reported figure carry the number of accepted outcomes it rests on, refuse to present a single observation as an average, and prove both with cases.

objects.title: Publish the cost-per-outcome claim with its unit defined beside it
objects.description: Move the cost-per-outcome claim to guaranteed, define the unit and the denominator where a reader meets the figure, and state what the number cannot be used to compare.

objects.title: Group comparable work from what the records already carry
objects.description: Derive the grouping that makes two pieces of work comparable from facts the records already hold, so that a recommendation compares like with like without anybody inventing a taxonomy of task types.

objects.title: Recommend a profile from measured cost, naming the measurements
objects.description: Add the command that recommends a profile for a class of work from measured cost per accepted outcome, and prints the measurements the recommendation was derived from alongside it.

objects.title: Return no recommendation where the data is too thin, and say why
objects.description: Make insufficient data produce no recommendation rather than a weak one, with the threshold declared as data and the reason printed, proved by cases on both sides of it.

objects.title: Prove the recommendation is advisory and publish it as such
objects.description: Prove with a case that a recommendation never changes the profile a task runs under, and publish the routing claim stating that Majordomus recommends and does not route.

objects.title: Let a policy name a shared source it does not copy
objects.description: Let a repository's policy name a shared policy source and resolve it offline from the filesystem, so that one statement of a rule can govern more than one repository without being pasted into each.

objects.title: Make a local override explicit and prove it survives an update of the shared source
objects.description: Define how a repository overrides part of a shared policy, require the override to be declared rather than inferred from a value differing, and prove with a case that updating the shared source leaves the override standing.

objects.title: Report drift from the shared policy in one command
objects.description: Report, in one command, every way a repository's effective policy differs from the shared source it names, separating declared overrides from undeclared divergence.

objects.title: Prove the offline guarantee survives sharing
objects.description: Prove with cases and a doctrine that no path introduced by shared policy reaches a network, and that an unavailable shared source degrades to a named refusal rather than a fetch or a silent local fallback.

objects.title: Publish the shared-policy claim and what sharing still cannot do
objects.description: Move the shared-policy claim to guaranteed, cite the implementation and the cases, and state plainly what a shared policy does not provide: no service, no registry, no cross-machine visibility, and no enforcement of a repository that never adopts it.

objects.title: Reproduce the misattribution as an executable case
objects.description: Write a behavioural case in which two workers share one checkout — one starts a task, the other records a decision — and assert what happens today, so that the defect stops being an anecdote and becomes something a command demonstrates.

objects.title: Decide how a record is attributed, between named alternatives
objects.description: Choose between the alternatives that actually exist — attribute to the session that ran the command, refuse to write when the active task belongs to somebody else, or require the task to be named explicitly — and record the choice with the case each rejected option gets wrong.

objects.title: Implement the decision and prove it holds
objects.description: Implement whatever I0702 decided across every command that writes a durable record, and turn the characterisation case into one that asserts the new behaviour.

objects.title: Publish what attribution guarantees, and what it still cannot
objects.description: State on the public surface what a record's attribution now means, and state plainly what it does not: that a worker's identity is supplied by the session, not verified, and that nothing here proves who a worker was.

objects.title: Narrow the Clean Extraction Boundary and record what was adopted
objects.description: Rewrite the Clean Extraction Boundary in docs/DESIGN.md so that it permits a generic deterministic provenance graph derived from this repository's own artifacts while continuing to exclude everything it excludes today, and record in docs/EXTRACTION_REPORT.md which architectural ideas from the studied prior art were adopted by re-derivation and which were refused, each with its reason.

objects.title: Specify the session record before writing one
objects.description: Define the session object in docs/SCHEMAS.md and docs/CONTINUITY.md: what a session is, how it differs from a task and from a handover, the filename grammar of a closed record, the exact field list, which fields are computed from git, and the rule that the reference envelope is derived rather than accumulated.

objects.title: Open a session and report its status
objects.description: Implement lib/session.sh with `session start` and `session status`: one active session per worktree in .majordomus/state/session-current.yaml, its identity and git facts computed, a second start refused rather than silently replacing the first, and a status that reports the active session against current git or says plainly that none is open.

objects.title: Close a session into an envelope derived from the ledger
objects.description: Implement `session close`: read the active record, derive the episode's references from the ledger between its start and now, write an immutable closed record with computed end-state git facts and an optional authored summary body, remove the active record, and append the close event to the ledger.

objects.title: Read sessions back with a divergence label
objects.description: Implement `session list`, `session show <id>` and `session latest`, each resolving with the established rule — same repository, same worktree, same branch, then same branch — and each printing the existing divergence label of the record against current git.

objects.title: Make the session rules doctrines, with retention and archiving
objects.description: Declare the session rules in share/standard/majordomus/ with validators that doctor and watch dispatch — a malformed active or closed record, a session left open past its policy, a reference to a record that does not exist, and retention over the declared cap — and implement policy-driven archiving that never deletes and never overwrites.

objects.title: Discover knowledge sources from git, not from the filesystem
objects.description: Implement the discovery stage of lib/knowledge.sh: a declared list of source classes, each with a scope of shared or operational, resolved through git ls-files for tracked repository artifacts and through the known state paths for operational records, producing a deterministic ordered list of sources with their content hashes.

objects.title: Extract nodes with identities that survive a rebuild
objects.description: Implement the extract and normalise stages in lib/knowledge.awk: one node per canonical object, with an identity derived from its canonical id or its repository path, a kind that is only asserted when a structural fact establishes it, and a title taken from the record or from the document's first heading.

objects.title: Record only edges that a file states, each with where it was observed
objects.description: Implement the resolve and graph stages: edges derived from the explicit relationships the canonical files already declare — claim to source, implementation and test; issue to milestone and to its dependencies; evidence to issue; doctrine to validator, claim and test; record to task — each carrying the file and field it was observed in, and none carrying a relationship inferred from prose.

objects.title: A content-hash manifest that makes a second sync cheap
objects.description: Implement the manifest: one row per source with its path, content hash, extractor version and the node ids it produced, written beside the generated graph, compared on every sync, and used so that a sync with no source change does no extraction and says so.

objects.title: Read-only knowledge lookup with an ordering that can be explained
objects.description: Implement `knowledge search`, `knowledge show` and `knowledge related`: deterministic lookup over the generated index with a documented, tested match order, JSON output that names the field each result matched on, and no write of any kind.

objects.title: Validate the graph, and let doctor and watch ask the same validator
objects.description: Implement `knowledge validate` detecting duplicate node ids, dangling explicit references, source paths that no longer exist, hash mismatches, edges with a missing end, edges without provenance and a stale generated index, each with a severity and a reproduce command, and declare the rule in the doctrine registry so doctor and watch dispatch the same validator rather than reimplementing it.

objects.title: A closed session becomes a node that points at its episode
objects.description: Extract closed sessions as knowledge nodes whose edges point at the tasks, issues, checkpoints, handovers, decisions and questions they name, so that the graph answers which sessions touched an issue, which decisions affected it, and which handover continued a task — without any session body being copied anywhere.

objects.title: Give the worker a bounded slice of knowledge, not the knowledge base
objects.description: Add a knowledge section to `majordomus context`, selected deterministically from what the active task and issue already reference, capped by a profile toggle and an item limit, dropped before any immutable fact when the budget is short, and named under EXCLUDED whenever it is dropped or switched off.

objects.title: Say what is now true in the claims, the documentation and the worker instructions
objects.description: Add the behavioural claims this milestone earns to docs/CLAIMS.yaml with real implementation and test paths, document the commands in docs/CLI.md, correct the sentence in docs/CONTINUITY.md that says no index is maintained, write docs/KNOWLEDGE.md, and extend the provider-neutral instruction source so a fresh worker knows the session and knowledge steps of the lifecycle.

objects.title: Prove the loop on a real issue, without a transcript
objects.description: Execute the whole lifecycle against a real issue of this repository — session start, plan next, plan show, context, knowledge retrieval, work, checkpoint and decision, evidence, plan done, session close, knowledge sync, watch — and record as evidence what a following session could determine from the records alone.

objects.title: Phase timing and work counters behind MJ_TIMING
objects.description: Time every validator and count every YAML flatten and git call when MJ_TIMING is set, and report them ranked at exit.

objects.title: The command registry is read in one pass
objects.description: Replace the per-index, per-field awk lookups in mj_cmdreg_public, mj_cmdreg_ids and the event registry with one awk pass each, and read them once per process.

objects.title: The project model is loaded with one flatten per file and no per-file lookups
objects.description: Make mj_project_load and mj_project_unknown_keys read each milestone and issue once, checking ids and unknown keys inside awk rather than with a subprocess per file and per key.

objects.title: Catalogue, DAG, context and command-surface validators read their inputs once
objects.description: Rewrite the remaining validators that loop mj_yget or mj_git per item so that each reads its inputs with one pass.

objects.title: Flattened YAML is cached under .ai/local/cache by content hash
objects.description: Cache the output of mj_yaml_flatten under .ai/local/cache/flat/<sha256>, keyed by the file's content hash and the flattener's own version, so a second command on unchanged files does no parsing.

objects.title: Every canonical file is flattened at most once per command
objects.description: Add a case that runs doctor, watch, context and plan validate under MJ_TIMING and asserts the yaml_flatten count never exceeds the number of distinct canonical files a command reads.

objects.title: majordomus bench: targets derived from the command registry
objects.description: Add the bench command: every public command in share/commands.yaml is a target, run against a disposable installed repository, with warmup and samples from the policy, reporting min, p50, p90, p95, p99, max, mean and stddev per target and mode.

objects.title: Bench persists local runs and keeps a latest projection
objects.description: Write every run to .ai/local/benchmarks/runs/<run-id>.json and .ai/local/benchmarks/latest.json atomically, and append one line per run to history.jsonl.

objects.title: An explicit committed baseline
objects.description: Add bench --write-baseline, which refuses a dirty tree unless forced, prints old, new and delta per target, and writes .ai/repo/benchmarks/baseline.json with schema majordomus/benchmark-baseline/v1.

objects.title: bench --check refuses a regression by policy
objects.description: Compare a fresh run against the baseline under the policy's benchmark.regression thresholds (relative p50, p95, p99) and exit non-zero naming the command, the metric, both values and the threshold.

objects.title: The benchmark policy block
objects.description: Declare benchmark.samples, benchmark.warmup, benchmark.timeout_seconds, benchmark.cache_max_entries, benchmark.regression.p50/p95/p99 and benchmark.budget.doctor_ms in the policy, its allow-list and the skeleton, with no reader-side default.

objects.title: doctor under a declared budget, and the hook inherits it
objects.description: Report doctor's own wall time against benchmark.budget.doctor_ms as a finding, advisory, and record the measured value on this repository as the budget's rationale in docs/PERFORMANCE.md.

objects.title: Performance doctrine as project rules
objects.description: Add project rules: derived state is computed once per state version, a command's hot path does not re-parse canonical files, every public command is benchmarkable from the registry, cacheability never changes observable behaviour, and performance claims need benchmark evidence.

objects.title: docs/PERFORMANCE.md, README, CONTRIBUTING and CLI reference
objects.description: Write the reference: goals, phases and counters, batch reads, the flatten cache, cold versus warm, result and baseline schemas, the policy block, the regression workflow, the contributor workflow and the limitations; add the README section and the bench section of docs/CLI.md.

objects.title: Performance claims at their proven status
objects.description: Add claims to docs/CLAIMS.yaml for derived benchmark targets, separated cold and warm distributions, flatten-once, cache equivalence and regression refusal, each naming its case, and regenerate the site data.

objects.title: generate-site-data instrumented and its hot spots removed
objects.description: Declare phases per section of the site generator, rank them, and remove the repeated work in the two most expensive sections.

objects.title: knowledge nodes and edges read each source once
objects.description: Time the knowledge stages, then remove the per-file subprocesses in discovery and extraction so that nodes and edges take one pass per source.

objects.title: The test runner reports per-case time and the suite budget
objects.description: Print each case's wall time in test/run.sh, sort the slowest at the end, and record the suite's total in the benchmark history as a system target.

objects.title: CI runs the structural performance checks
objects.description: Add the flatten-once case, the cache-equivalence case and bench --check with the CI profile to validate.yml, with the wall-clock thresholds conservative and the counters exact.

objects.title: A synthetic repository generator for scaling cases
objects.description: Add a test helper that builds a repository with N issues, N milestones, N rules and N context documents from the skeleton, and a case that runs doctor and plan validate at three sizes and asserts the yaml_flatten count grows linearly.

objects.title: Timing report as JSON
objects.description: Under --json, print the timing report as one JSON object on stderr with phases and counters, so bench can carry a phase breakdown per sample.

objects.title: bench compare and the top regressions report
objects.description: Add bench compare <run-a> <run-b> and make the human report rank the largest regressions, the largest improvements and the slowest targets by p95.

objects.title: watch inherits every doctor fix and its own budget
objects.description: Confirm watch dispatches the rewritten validators, time it, and declare benchmark.budget.watch_ms next to doctor's.

objects.title: context and its subcommands under a second
objects.description: Time context resolve, validate, affected and check-sync, and remove the per-document git and awk calls so each runs under a second on this repository.

objects.title: Cache equivalence proved by property-shaped cases
objects.description: For every read-only command in the registry, run it with the cache cold, warm, and disabled, on this repository and on a synthetic one, and assert byte-identical output and exit code; then mutate one file and assert the changed output is served.

objects.title: Before and after evidence for every optimisation
objects.description: Record, for each hot spot removed, the phase time before and after and the counter before and after, in the benchmark history and in the commit message, and summarise them in docs/PERFORMANCE.md by pointing at the baseline file.

objects.title: The performance workflow is discoverable and complete
objects.description: Close the milestone: every acceptance criterion of M004 has evidence, the README workflow runs as written, the site is regenerated, and the final report is a plan record rather than a conversation.

objects.title: Milestone and DAG driven development
objects.description: Every non-trivial change in this repository belongs to a milestone specification and to one dependency-linked issue execution contract, validated as a DAG, with status derived rather than asserted, and projected to GitHub and to the website from that one canonical model.

objects.title: A blocking question survives a handover
objects.description: An unresolved question keeps refusing a completed finish after the work moves to a new task, or the alternative is chosen deliberately and the reason is recorded where the next worker will read it.

objects.title: A durable record names the worker that wrote it
objects.description: A durable record either names the worker that produced it or is refused, and a record written from one session can never arrive attributed to another session's task.

objects.title: A session is a durable envelope, and knowledge is compiled from what is already canonical
objects.description: A worker with no conversation history can answer what happened, why, what was decided, which evidence supports it, where the canonical source lives, and what to do next — from records and a derived index, with git still the authority over both.

objects.title: Performance is executable evidence, and the hot path does no canonical work twice
objects.description: Every public command can be benchmarked from the command registry with cold and warm distributions, the phases and work counters of any run can be printed, the caches and batch reads that remove repeated work preserve every observable result, an accepted baseline lives in the repository and a check refuses a regression by policy, and the pre-commit hook is fast enough that nobody routes around it.

objects.title: Cost per accepted outcome, only on measured data
objects.description: The cost of an accepted outcome is computed from measured telemetry and the finish contract that accepted it, and is reported only where both exist.

objects.title: Execution telemetry, only from providers that expose it honestly
objects.description: Execution telemetry is recorded for providers that report it truthfully, and absence is recorded as absence rather than estimated.

objects.title: A supervisory control layer that is real rather than described
objects.description: A repository carries one policy, a small set of profiles, durable task state, and a set of commands that refuse work which does not meet a declared contract — with every rule dispatched from a registry that proves it reaches the command claiming to run it.

objects.title: Routing recommendations derived from measured cost
objects.description: The profile a task should run under is recommended from measured cost per accepted outcome, and the recommendation names the data it came from.

objects.title: Profiles become runtime constraints rather than advice
objects.description: A profile's axes become opt-in runtime clamps a provider actually applies — read size, output condensation, subagent budget — with the limit derived from the profile rather than configured twice.

objects.title: Shared policy across repositories and workers
objects.description: A policy can be shared across repositories and workers, with local override remaining explicit and drift from the shared source detectable in one command.

objects.title: debugging
objects.description: reproduce, isolate, fix, and prove a defect fixed

objects.title: deep-work
objects.description: design, architecture, cross-cutting change, or a problem with no known shape

objects.title: implementation
objects.description: build a described feature or change within a known design

objects.title: routine
objects.description: small, well-understood changes; rename, bump, wording, one-line fixes

objects.title: continue
objects.description: resume a task from durable state instead of from someone's memory

objects.title: debug
objects.description: frame a defect so that the fix is proven, not asserted

objects.title: handover
objects.description: produce a continuation record body for the current task

objects.title: review
objects.description: review the working diff against the claimed scope and the finish contract

objects.title: Architecture decision integrity
objects.description: Every architecture decision the repository holds parses against the decision contract, claims an identity nothing else claims, and every relation and reference it makes resolves.

objects.title: AI layer integrity
objects.description: The repository's AI layer is real: the manifest declares a format this executable reads and every section it names exists, the checkout-local half is ignored by git and nothing under it is tracked, and no project data remains under the pre-.ai .majordomus/ path.

objects.title: Blocker resolution
objects.description: No task can be completed while any question on this branch is unresolved; it can still be finished as blocked, partial, no_match or failed.

objects.title: Bootstrap integrity
objects.description: The path from a human reader to the AI layer is unbroken — README.md names AGENTS.md, every generated instruction file points at .ai/README.md, and none of them carries a rule of its own.

objects.title: Catalogue integrity
objects.description: Every use case and application describes the tool in terms the tool has — each command, doctrine and claim it names exists, and the two catalogues reference each other in both directions.

objects.title: Checkpoint freshness
objects.description: A task whose last checkpoint is older than its profile's interval is reported, not stopped.

objects.title: Every public command is exercised and refuted
objects.description: Every public command has a behavioural test and a negative test, computed from the registry and the coverage each case declares about itself rather than from a list someone maintains.

objects.title: The command surface is declared and reconciled
objects.description: Every command the binary dispatches is described by the shipped registry, every command the registry declares public is dispatched, and a command is public exactly when the usage text lists it.

objects.title: Context budget
objects.description: The always-loaded projection stays within its line budget, every reference in it resolves, it states no count that will go stale, and the assembled context fits the builder's own budget.

objects.title: Context integrity
objects.description: The scoped context documents under the AI layer carry the context contract, compose into one deterministic chain for every path, and a tree that does not validate resolves nothing.

objects.title: Dependency graph integrity
objects.description: The issue dependency graph is acyclic, every edge names an issue that exists, and no issue is executing ahead of a dependency that is not done.

objects.title: Decision records
objects.description: Every entry in decisions.md carries the task, the head and the reason, so a decision can be found by the worker who needs it.

objects.title: Define done before executing
objects.description: The finish contract is evaluated line by line, and nothing else counts as done.

objects.title: Execution depth is not output verbosity
objects.description: Think as hard as the task needs; report as briefly as the profile says.

objects.title: Doctrine wiring integrity
objects.description: Every doctrine in this registry resolves to a validator that exists, is reached from every command it names, propagates failure, is proved by a test, and is run by CI — and every validator in the source is declared here.

objects.title: Enforcement wiring
objects.description: Every enforcement the policy declares is invoked by the hook it names, from a file the dispatcher will actually execute, without swallowing the exit code.

objects.title: Externalise decisions and durable state
objects.description: A decision you make goes into a record, dated, with what was rejected and why; a question for a person goes into the questions store.

objects.title: Handover integrity
objects.description: The resolver runs and reports either the record for this worktree and branch or its clean absence; a malformed record is never silently skipped, and a record describing a history this checkout no longer has is reported.

objects.title: Handovers transfer state, not transcripts
objects.description: A handover says what is true now and the one next action; never conversation history.

objects.title: Parallel work requires isolation
objects.description: Do not start a second task in a checkout that already has one; overlapping claims across worktrees are reported.

objects.title: Escalate capability and effort only when justified
objects.description: The profile sets the default capability and effort; escalation is recorded, never assumed.

objects.title: Layout integrity
objects.description: The directories the durable commands write into are installed rather than created on first use.

objects.title: Ledger integrity
objects.description: Every line of the append-only ledger is a well-formed event; the one durable record nothing else can reconstruct stays readable.

objects.title: Load minimum sufficient context
objects.description: The profile says what to load; discover everything that may apply and load only what does.

objects.title: Note integrity
objects.description: Every outcome needs a note carrying the sections that outcome requires, and no transcript.

objects.title: One worker, one clear scope
objects.description: A task claims the paths it may touch, and touches only those.

objects.title: Policy completeness
objects.description: Every policy value the code reads is declared in the skeleton policy, and no reader carries its own default for one.

objects.title: Policy integrity
objects.description: The policy and every profile parse, declare version 1, and carry no key the schema does not define.

objects.title: Profile requirements
objects.description: A profile may demand more than the shared contract — a regression test, a decision record — and finish refuses without it.

objects.title: Project model integrity
objects.description: Every milestone and issue file parses, carries the id its filename claims, and contains no key nobody reads.

objects.title: Projection integrity
objects.description: Every generated instruction file exists, matches the stamp it carries, and is never silently overwritten after a hand edit.

objects.title: Prompt capture is proven, or reported unavailable
objects.description: A repository that declares prompt capture has it wired below the model and proven by running it; the archive stays ignored and untracked, every prompt is present as both a record and a rendering, and neither carries anything the model said.

objects.title: Prompt integrity
objects.description: Every repository-local prompt asset renders, and every token in it is one the renderer knows.

objects.title: Questions store integrity
objects.description: Every entry in open-questions.md parses, because a gate that cannot read an entry can be bypassed by mistyping one.

objects.title: Retention caps
objects.description: The ledger and the handover directory stay under the caps the policy sets, so durable state does not grow without bound.

objects.title: The roadmap is a projection, never a document
objects.description: No document is a second authority for the roadmap. While a hand-written roadmap table exists, it can neither list a version no milestone declares nor hide one the model does.

objects.title: Rule package integrity
objects.description: The repository's effective rule set is real: the vendored baseline matches its manifest file for file, every rule resolves with its dependencies and no two claim one identity, and no project rule reuses the vendored namespace.

objects.title: Scope integrity
objects.description: A task touches only the paths it claimed; work found elsewhere is not accepted as done.

objects.title: Sessions are workers, not memory
objects.description: Durable state lives in records the repository keeps, never in a conversation.

objects.title: Skill integrity
objects.description: Every skill the repository declares parses against the skill contract, names the directory it lives in, carries its sections, and every skill or example it refers to exists.

objects.title: State consistency
objects.description: The task record still describes this checkout — same branch, and HEAD at or ahead of the recorded commit.

objects.title: Task continuity
objects.description: A task finished as partial or blocked should leave a handover record, not only a note section.

objects.title: Use-case coverage
objects.description: Every public command, and every guaranteed claim and MCP tool the policy asks for, is named and run by at least one active use case whose scenario executes against the real tool; a gap is a failure or a report according to the policy, never silence.

objects.title: Verification integrity
objects.description: Completion requires a verification command that actually ran and exited 0; its exit code and duration are recorded.

objects.title: Verify outcomes, not activity
objects.description: A test that ran and passed is evidence; a sentence saying it did is not.

objects.title: Every public command is benchmarkable from the registry
objects.description: The benchmark targets are the public commands of share/commands.yaml and their scenarios are the command fixtures; no second list of what to time exists, and a command whose fixture the harness cannot run is a defect of the fixture, not an exemption.

objects.title: Blocking checks are deterministic and cheap
objects.description: A check that can stop a command is deterministic and cheap; work in progress is reported, never blocked.

objects.title: A cache never changes what a command observes
objects.description: A cache of derived state, if one exists, is keyed by the version of the canonical state it derives from, is bypassable, and produces byte-identical output to the uncached path; a cache that can be observed through a command's output, exit code or findings is a defect, and a cache that no case proves equivalent does not exist.

objects.title: Clean room
objects.description: The Prismatic name is the only thing carried from anywhere else: no internal paths, hostnames, component names, doctrine vocabulary or quotations.

objects.title: Context locality
objects.description: Context lives in the narrowest directory scope where it stays correct; root files bootstrap and link, provider files are projections.

objects.title: Conventional commits, committed and pushed incrementally
objects.description: Commits use the conventional format type(scope): description with the co-author footer the session provides, and land incrementally rather than as one large change.

objects.title: Derived files are regenerated, never edited
objects.description: A generated file is changed by changing its canonical source and rerunning the generator, and both are committed together.

objects.title: Derived state is computed once per state version
objects.description: Anything derivable solely from unchanged canonical repository state is computed once per version of that state and read many times; a command's hot path does not rediscover, reparse or rebuild it per item, per request or per call.

objects.title: English only
objects.description: Code, comments, commits, documents and governance records are written in English, with no exceptions.

objects.title: Every finding carries a reproduce command
objects.description: Every finding a command reports names the command that reproduces it.

objects.title: A command reads each canonical file at most once
objects.description: Within one invocation a command flattens, hashes or parses a canonical file at most once, however many validators, accessors or projections need it; the second reader gets the first reading.

objects.title: External interfaces are projections of one capability definition
objects.description: A capability is defined once, as a typed descriptor in Rust or as a declarative object with its schema in the layer, and MCP, HTTP, OpenAPI, Swagger UI, CLI introspection and the generated reference are derived from it.

objects.title: A native command line command exists only with its documentation and its executable examples
objects.description: Every command of the Rust executable is declared once in clap with the examples beside it, every command a person can run carries at least one example that the crate's tests execute against the built binary, and the generated reference, the site dataset and the routes under /docs/cli/ are projections that CI refuses to let go stale.

objects.title: Never author identity fields
objects.description: repository_id, branch, head, working_tree and changed_files on any record are computed from git and never written by hand.

objects.title: Never store or summarise transcripts
objects.description: No record stores or summarises a conversation; records carry what is true now and the next action.

objects.title: No claim without a test
objects.description: A capability sentence in README.md or docs/ is backed by a case in test/cases/ or is phrased as a target.

objects.title: No counts in prose
objects.description: Prose never states a number the repository can compute; it states the command that computes it.

objects.title: No network, no telemetry, no eval, no silent overwrite, no recursive deletion
objects.description: bin/, lib/, share/ and test/ contain no network client, no telemetry, no eval, no curl piped to a shell, no silent overwrite and no recursive deletion outside a temporary directory.

objects.title: No new nouns
objects.description: The tool gains no agents, personas, roles, tiers or registries beyond the vocabulary it has.

objects.title: Complexity is optional, not ambient
objects.description: Simple things are trivial, complex things possible, weird things hackable; a change that makes the default path harder, adds a foundational noun without a concrete need, or leaks internals into ordinary use is refused in review.

objects.title: A performance claim carries its measurement
objects.description: A change made for speed names the phase or counter it changed and both values, measured on this repository with the tool's own timing; a budget or a threshold is set from a run, never guessed; a baseline is a tracked file written by the harness and updated on purpose.

objects.title: Portable shell
objects.description: bash 3.2 and BSD userland are the floor: no associative arrays, no mapfile, no GNU-only flags, and shellcheck -x -s bash passes on every script.

objects.title: A new enforced rule is a doctrine, not an inline check
objects.description: A rule the tool enforces is declared as a rule object with an x-majordomus block and a validator named mj_validate_<name>; no command selects checks by hand.

objects.title: No endpoint of the Rust executable without a benchmark, and no number without evidence
objects.description: Every externally callable operation of the Rust executable (each executable capability directly and on every transport its exposure declares, and the transports' own operations) is a benchmark target with a denominator generated from the registry; coverage is complete or the structural check fails; a waiver is typed, reported and never counted; and a claim about latency is made from a recorded measurement, never from prose.

objects.title: One canonical declaration; modules compose capabilities; the root composes modules
objects.description: An executable capability of the Rust executable is declared once with capability!, composed into its module with module!, and the application composes modules with compose_modules!; every interface, benchmark target, cache behaviour and generated document is derived from that declaration, and editing a projection to add or change one is a defect.

objects.title: The Rust executable carries its evidence with it
objects.description: Every capability and every documented behaviour of apps/majordomus-cli is proved by a behavioural test, every public item is documented with an executable example where one is meaningful, line coverage stays above the threshold CI enforces, and the hot paths carry benchmarks.

objects.title: A request never rebuilds canonical state, and a cache is never trusted without an equivalence test
objects.description: After the Rust executable has started, no MCP or HTTP request scans the repository, builds the index or the registry, derives a schema or builds a projection; every call goes through the one executor; a cache exists only where a measurement justified it, is bounded, is keyed by the registry fingerprint, and is proved to answer what the handler answers.

objects.title: What a worker reads is declared once, and nothing outside it is read or served
objects.description: The repository scope, the pathspecs a worker reads and the paths, names, sizes and content it never reads, is declared once as data in .ai/repo/scope.yaml (or the distribution's default when a repository declares none), and the Rust executable discovers, indexes and serves nothing outside it, answers for any path whether it is in or out and why, and reports a tracked secret.

objects.title: Nothing a client leaves behind locks another client out
objects.description: The shared MCP server is a client's child; whatever state a client or a dead server leaves behind is taken over or bypassed, and a client that cannot share is served alone, never turned away.

objects.title: Tests run in disposable repositories
objects.description: Behavioural cases run through bash test/run.sh in a temporary repository each, never against this checkout.

objects.title: Unknown configuration keys are errors
objects.description: Every configuration file rejects a key nothing reads, and every state field is both written and read.

objects.title: A use case is proved by execution, and a capability is covered by a use case
objects.description: Every externally meaningful capability of this repository is demonstrated by an active use case whose scenario executes against the real tool; every example a page shows comes from that execution; a use case's maturity is observed, never authored; and a change to a command, rule, claim, provider, MCP tool, schema, application or workflow runs use-case impact analysis before the work is called complete.

objects.title: Deploy the site by hand
objects.description: Publish the website to GitHub Pages from a terminal, through the one script the Pages workflow runs, when waiting for the Actions queue is not acceptable.

objects.title: Implement a change
objects.description: Carry a requested change through the repository evidence-first, from the invariant it must keep to a verified, reconciled, documented and committed tree, without widening its scope.

objects.title: Repository review
objects.description: An evidence-driven review of the actual state of the repository, or of one change to it, before meaningful engineering work is recommended or done.

objects.title: Getting started and adoption
objects.description: Bringing Majordomus into a repository, new or old, without losing what people already wrote.

objects.title: Completion and quality gates
objects.description: Deciding whether work is finished, with a contract every line of which passes or fails.

objects.title: Sessions and handover
objects.description: Stopping and resuming work across sessions and workers from durable state, never a transcript.

objects.title: Drift and reconciliation
objects.description: Detecting that policy, projections, state and git disagree, and putting them back in step.

objects.title: Extension
objects.description: Adding a kind, a rule, a command or a use case as data, with the checks that follow from it.

objects.title: Repository knowledge
objects.description: What the repository declares about itself: sources, nodes, edges, the plan, and searching them.

objects.title: Serving the layer to AI clients
objects.description: One shared server per repository, every client a peer, the same layer over MCP, HTTP and the command line.

objects.title: Performance
objects.description: Benchmarks derived from the registry, baselines that are data, and budgets doctor reports against.

objects.title: Policy and enforcement
objects.description: Declaring rules, proving they are wired, and reproducing a finding.

objects.title: Parallel workers
objects.description: Several agents or people on one repository: claimed scopes, overlap, and who touched what.

objects.title: Decide whether finished work is actually finished
objects.description: Evaluate a contract line by line instead of accepting a sentence that says the work is done.

objects.title: Add a use case and let the tool prove it
objects.description: Scaffold a draft for an uncovered command, validate it, run its scenario against the real tool, and see the coverage move.

objects.title: Adopt a repository that already has its own rules
objects.description: Install the supervisory layer into a repository with a hand-written CLAUDE.md, without the tool taking ownership of a file somebody else wrote.

objects.title: Block acceptance on a question nobody has answered
objects.description: Open a question against the task, watch finish refuse completion while it is unresolved, resolve it with the answer, and only then complete.

objects.title: Keep the prompts that started the work, below the model rather than around it
objects.description: Wire the provider hook, prove it by running a payload through it, and see that a prompt the tool could not parse is reported rather than silently dropped.

objects.title: Hand work over with a question still open, and keep it blocking
objects.description: Close a task into a handover while a question is unresolved, start the follow-up task, and see the same question still refuse acceptance there.

objects.title: Checkpoint long work so a stop costs minutes, not the day
objects.description: Record compact progress inside the active task at the profile interval, so a session that ends without warning leaves the next one a place to start.

objects.title: Decide what belongs in the AI context, as data
objects.description: Read the repository’s declared scope policy, see which paths are in and out of the index, and let doctor and the knowledge index apply it rather than a hardcoded list.

objects.title: Complete an issue only when its evidence exists
objects.description: See an issue refuse completion while a required piece of evidence is missing, read the roadmap the milestone state derives, and keep the GitHub projection a projection.

objects.title: Deliver issues in waves the graph computes, and take the next one
objects.description: Validate the plan, read the execution waves the dependency graph yields, see which issues are ready and which are blocked on what, and take the one issue a worker should do now.

objects.title: Extend what the executable serves by adding a file, never by rebuilding it
objects.description: Add a rule, a prompt or a knowledge node to .ai/ and have it appear as an MCP resource, an HTTP route and a reference entry, with the same binary.

objects.title: Find an object of the layer without reading everything
objects.description: Search durable records literally across kinds from the shell, and ask the shared server the same question over MCP with majordomus_search and majordomus_get.

objects.title: Find out what has drifted since anyone last looked
objects.description: Ask what has moved, rather than whether anything is wrong.

objects.title: Follow a procedure the repository defines, and add another one
objects.description: Read the repository''s skills, take one as it is written, and add a new one by writing its file — no registry, no code, and a check that says what it examined.

objects.title: Gate CI on the tool itself, with an exit code that is a contract
objects.description: Run the checks CI runs, read every finding with the command that reproduces it, and rely on exit codes that mean one thing each: no code means warn and continue.

objects.title: Hand unfinished work to the next session
objects.description: Stop mid-task and leave the next worker something to act on that is not a transcript.

objects.title: Record a decision so the next worker can find it
objects.description: Write down what was decided and why as state, then find it again without reading a conversation.

objects.title: Keep every provider bootstrap thin, generated and within budget
objects.description: Regenerate AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and the other provider files from one policy and prove they are stamped, point at the layer, stay under the line budget and resolve every reference.

objects.title: Check the version before trusting a diagnosis
objects.description: Print the version every other surface derives from, and see the argument it refuses.

objects.title: Move a repository from the pre-.ai layout to the layer
objects.description: See what a migration would move, move it with a backup, and prove the result is a layer the tool reads.

objects.title: Record what one worker did in one sitting
objects.description: Open a session, do the work under whatever tasks it touches, and close it into an envelope that references what it produced and copies nothing.

objects.title: Keep the plan as milestones and issues the tool can validate
objects.description: Declare milestones as outcomes and issues as execution contracts, and let the tool say what is ready and what is blocked.

objects.title: Prove a rule is actually enforced, not merely written down
objects.description: Answer "is this rule real?" with a command rather than a reading of the source.

objects.title: Prove the tool is fast, not assume it, and refuse a regression
objects.description: Measure every public command and every capability of the executable against a committed baseline, and let the check fail on a regression rather than a reviewer noticing later.

objects.title: Read back what happened, and keep the ledger within its cap
objects.description: Read the append-only ledger as operational history, filtered by task and event, validate every line, and rotate the oldest lines into an archive rather than deleting them.

objects.title: Read only the context that fits the budget, and know what was dropped
objects.description: Assemble the context a worker needs now in authority order, cut it to a line budget, and see every dropped section named with its reason.

objects.title: See which rules apply here and what enforces them
objects.description: List the effective rule set, read one rule as the tool reads it, and see which of them the tool enforces and from where.

objects.title: Record a decision as data, and prove the tool cannot accept it for you
objects.description: Read the decisions a repository holds, validate the whole set in one command, and watch the tool refuse to write the one status only a person may write.

objects.title: Start a session from a rendered framing, not a pasted transcript
objects.description: List the prompt assets the repository ships, render one against the durable state, and read the context it embeds.

objects.title: Resume in the right worktree, never against somebody else’s task
objects.description: Find the handover that belongs to this worktree and branch, and see a task record from another checkout reported as foreign rather than enforced here.

objects.title: Run several workers in one repository without them colliding
objects.description: Give each worker a declared scope, and find out immediately when two of them claim the same paths.

objects.title: Serve the repository's AI layer to every AI client through one shared server
objects.description: Open the repository in Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI and have each of them read the same rules, prompts and knowledge over MCP from one process, seeing each other.

objects.title: Trace a change to the context documents it affects
objects.description: List the scoped context documents, resolve which apply to a path and why, and find out which documents a change set touches before it lands.

objects.title: Trust the policy and the profiles only after they are validated
objects.description: Prove that the canonical policy parses with every key it needs declared, that every profile parses and the default exists, and that what the policy declares as enforced is what actually runs.

cli.about: Majordomus control plane: a data-driven MCP server over the repository's .ai/ layer
cli.long_about:
The Rust executable of Majordomus. It reads the repository's provider-neutral AI layer under .ai/ and serves it, read-only, to MCP clients over stdio.

The task lifecycle (init, start, check, finish, doctor, ...) is the shell tool bin/majordomus in the same repository; this executable does not implement those commands.

tools.name: majordomus_capability
tools.title: Describe one capability
tools.description: One capability by canonical id: its kind, schemas, provenance, stability, exposures, benchmark and cache policy.

tools.name: majordomus_capabilities
tools.title: List capabilities
tools.description: Every capability of this executable and this repository, summarised: kind, module, stability, provenance, the projections it declares, its benchmark and cache policy; the schemas are answered by capabilities.describe.

tools.name: majordomus_get
tools.title: Get one object
tools.description: One object by URI (majordomus://<kind>/<identity>): metadata, provenance and content; a URI a query projects (majordomus://repository) answers that query as a JSON document. The same resolution serves the MCP resource read.

tools.name: majordomus_list
tools.title: List objects
tools.description: List the declarative objects of the repository's AI layer, optionally by kind or tag.

tools.name: majordomus_search
tools.title: Search objects
tools.description: Case-insensitive substring search over identities, titles, descriptions and content.

tools.name: majordomus_announce
tools.title: Announce what this peer is working on
tools.description: Tell the other peers of this shared server what the calling session is doing and which paths it expects to touch. Changes this process's memory only; the repository is never written. Needs an MCP session: over plain HTTP there is no caller.

tools.name: majordomus_peers
tools.title: List peers
tools.description: Every client attached to this shared server: id, the client's own name and version from its initialize, transport, when it attached, when it was last seen, and what it announced. In-memory, gone with the process.

tools.name: majordomus_perf
tools.title: Performance counters
tools.description: The counters of this process: repository scans, index and registry builds, schema generations, projection builds, executions, handler invocations, cache hits, misses and evictions, and the phase timings, as they stand now.

tools.name: majordomus_repository
tools.title: Repository and index state
tools.description: The repository root, layer sections, git state, discovery mode, kinds present, every diagnostic, and the capability registry counted.

tools.name: majordomus_scope
tools.title: The repository scope
tools.description: The scope declaration as read, where it came from (the repository's own or the distribution's default), and every tracked file tallied against it: how many are in, how many are out for each reason, and which.

tools.name: majordomus_scope_classify
tools.title: Judge a path against the scope
tools.description: Whether a repository-relative path is in or out of the scope, the reason when it is out, and the pattern or limit that decided; an existing file is judged by name, then size, then content.
